about: Mini golden dataset (5 questions) for Phase 2 retrieval tuning against the EU digital-regulation demo corpus. Used manually to compare vector vs keyword vs hybrid retrieval while tuning chunk size, topK, and RRF, so Phase 2 decisions are measured rather than guessed.
seeds_phase_4: THESE 5 QUESTIONS SEED THE FULL PHASE 4 GOLDEN DATASET. Phase 4 ('Define golden dataset schema' and 'Create demo golden dataset', ~20 questions) expands this seed into the atlas-evals datasets/ directory convention (questions.jsonl + expected answers/chunks + difficulty tags). Keep the ids stable so results stay comparable across phases.
corpus: corpus/manifest.json — 29 EU digital-regulation PDFs fetched from EUR-Lex. Ingest with corpus/download.sh then corpus/ingest.sh before running the check.
usage: With the docker compose stack up and the corpus ingested, run atlas-evals/mini-golden-check.sh (needs curl + jq). For each answerable question it reports, per endpoint (/api/search/{vector,keyword,hybrid}), hit@5 and the rank of the first expected-document chunk. For the unanswerable question it reports the top score per endpoint (which should be low).

schema.id: stable identifier (do not renumber across phases)
schema.question: natural-language query POSTed to the search endpoints
schema.expected_document: filename from corpus/manifest.json, or null when the corpus cannot answer
schema.expected_pages: { from, to } inclusive 1-based page range, or an array of page numbers when the relevant pages are disjoint, or null
schema.notes: why this question is in the set / what it is meant to exercise

questions.question: What are the tasks of the data protection officer?
questions.notes: Keyword-heavy: the distinctive phrase 'data protection officer' and 'tasks' appear verbatim in GDPR Art 37-39 (pp. 55-56), so websearch_to_tsquery matches and keyword search ranks GDPR at #1 — as do vector and hybrid. Guards against a chunking/RRF change silently regressing exact-term retrieval.

questions.question: If software or a streaming service I paid for does not work as advertised, what can I demand from the trader?
questions.notes: Semantic paraphrase: the colloquial wording ('doesn't work as advertised', 'demand from the trader') shares almost no rare terms with the legal text ('conformity', 'remedies', Art 14, remedies pp. 22-25; conformity basis ~p. 13), so keyword search misses entirely while vector returns the Digital Content Directive across the whole top-5. The clearest vector-beats-keyword case in the set.

questions.question: How quickly must an essential-services operator notify authorities after a serious security incident?
questions.notes: Incident-notification timelines appear across several cybersecurity instruments. NIS2 (Art 23, 24h early warning / 72h notification, pp. 49-51) is the primary/current source; nis1.pdf (the predecessor, ~pp. 20-22) is an acceptable secondary, and dora.pdf / cra.pdf carry ICT- and product-specific reporting. expected_document is the primary — Phase 4 should credit all acceptable sources.

questions.question: What must the crypto-asset white paper for an asset-referenced token contain?
questions.notes: Hard: precise MiCA jargon ('asset-referenced token', 'crypto-asset white paper') buried in a 166-page document, and the full-sentence phrasing defeats keyword search (all content words must co-occur in one chunk). Vector and hybrid rank MiCA #1; keyword returns nothing. Exercises retrieval precision on the largest document (further detail lives in annexes ~pp. 148-153).

questions.question: What is the recommended daily amount of water an adult should drink?
questions.notes: Out-of-corpus (health/nutrition, not EU digital regulation). The top vector score should be low (~0.2 observed) versus ~0.77 for answerable questions — the signal a Phase 4 abstention check would threshold on. Note: topically-adjacent unanswerables (e.g. US HIPAA/CCPA) score higher (~0.5) because the corpus's US adequacy decisions overlap, so this seed deliberately uses a clean off-domain case.

questions.question: What does the AI Act consider a high-risk AI system?
questions.notes: Known-hard query that exists to permanently track a fusion behaviour. The Article 6 high-risk classification chunks are indexes 38 (p. 14, classifying recital), 138 (pp. 53-54), and 139/141/142 (pp. 54-56). CORRECTION (verified via GET /api/chunks): index 138 is a DEFINITIONAL chunk — it contains Article 6(1)-(3), the classification test itself. It merely OPENS with the tail of Article 5 (annual reporting on real-time remote biometric identification), which is all its 300-char snippet shows; an earlier analysis mistook the snippet for the whole chunk and wrongly labelled 138 a term-dense distractor. Vector correctly ranks 138 #1. Keyword's AND-semantics never surface it (the query's content words don't all co-occur), so it appears in the vector list only; hybrid RRF therefore demotes it out of the top 5 as a single-engine result. That is a mild fusion cost, not a win: hybrid's top 4 are still the other Article-6 chunks (38, 142, 139, 141). The regression signal is thus FLIPPED — an engine or fusion config that drops index 138 from the top 5 is losing the single best chunk. Expected chunk indexes for future page-level matching: 138 joins 38/139/141/142.
